newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Q3 tax revenues up 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Israel Q3 tax revenues up 2.5 pct.

text.p: Israel's Treasury said on Sunday tax revenues in the third quarter of the year rose a real 2.5 percent to 24.6 billion shekels from 21.5 billion shekels in the year-earlier quarter.
Revenue from income and property taxes in the quarter rose one percent while revenue from customs and value added tax (VAT) increased five percent to 10.9 billion shekels.
In the first nine months of the year total tax revenues rose by a real three percent to 70.9 billion shekels from 61.8 billion shekels a year earlier.
The Treasury said that if not for changes in tax legislation and certain other factors the increase would have been five percent.
Income and property taxes fell by one percent in the first nine months to 38.8 billion shekels while customs and VAT revenues rose six percent to 31.5 billion shekels.
The Treasury did not reveal figures for September but officials said revenues were in line with forecast, unlike in August when revenues fell short of forecast.
Revenues since the beginning of the year are also well below forecast although officials would not disclose the Treasury's forecast.

One reason for the shortfall is that the Treasury did not accurately calculate the implications of certain tax changes, an official said. Also, it appears that the forecast had been overly optimistic from the start, he said.
